novel_features.name: Customer Intel Deep
novel_features.description: A one-screen, time-ordered timeline for a customer joining Slack mentions, the Attio deal stage at that moment, open Asana tasks, and Fathom call action items — every line cited with a permalink.
novel_features.rationale: Requires four co-located SQLite mirrors (pp-slack, pp-attio, pp-asana, pp-fathom) and an ATTACH DATABASE join no MCP or single API call can produce.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an alert fires and you need the full cross-source history of a customer in one call, not Slack chatter alone.

novel_features.name: DM Engagement
novel_features.description: One volume row per direct report: DM count with you, Asana tasks created and completed, and Fathom calls attended over a time window.
novel_features.rationale: A three-mirror join across pp-slack, pp-asana, and pp-fathom that no single Slack API call spans.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before 1:1s or scorecard reviews to see real engagement volumes per report instead of scrolling DMs.

novel_features.name: Action Follow-through
novel_features.description: For each Fathom call action item assigned to a CSM, whether that person mentioned the company in Slack within the window — with the matching permalink when they did.
novel_features.rationale: pp-fathom owns the action items and pp-slack owns the full-text search of mentions; the join only works with both mirrors local.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in L10 prep to audit whether commitments made on calls were actually acted on.

novel_features.name: Goal Channel Pulse
novel_features.description: Per active Asana Rock in the current quarter, the mapped Slack channel's 7-day message count, unique participants, total reactions, and a stalled flag when discussion is zero.
novel_features.rationale: Joins pp-asana goal data with pp-slack message data co-located on disk — a conversation-level signal beyond pp-asana's task-level drift.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in L10 prep to see whether the team is actually talking about each Rock, not just whether tasks moved.

novel_features.name: Reactions Summarize
novel_features.description: Aggregates emoji reactions across every message in a channel over a window: top messages by reaction count, emoji distribution, and a fixed emoji-class bucket count.
novel_features.rationale: A mechanical GROUP BY over the local reactions table joined to messages; the MCP returns per-message reactions only, so cross-message aggregation costs N round-trips.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for a daily attention pulse on which messages drew the most team reaction.

novel_features.name: Unreads Priority
novel_features.description: An inventory of unread DMs, at-mentions, and involved threads, bucketed by priority — DM over partner channel over internal channel over broadcast — with per-bucket counts.
novel_features.rationale: Scans the local mirror's per-channel last-read cursor against message timestamps; a window-based attention sweep cannot produce a read-now shape.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as the morning triage of what actually needs reading right now.

novel_features.name: Usergroups Render
novel_features.description: Lists usergroups with handle and members, and renders subteam mentions in all output as readable @handles instead of raw <!subteam^S...> IDs.
novel_features.rationale: Needs a local usergroups lookup table and an emit-time substitution pass; fixes a known mis-render bug in the weekly-digest workflow.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use so digests and channel reads render subteam mentions as human handles, not opaque IDs.

novel_features.name: Agent Audit
novel_features.description: Shows which agents and cron jobs read which Slack DMs and channels over a window, sourced from the CLI's own append-only DM-read audit log.
novel_features.rationale: A read over pp-slack's own audit_log table — no other tool can see which automated callers touched DM data.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for privacy governance — to know which automated agents accessed DM content.

narrative.headline: Every Slack Web API endpoint, plus a local SQLite mirror that unlocks compound queries and cross-source customer timelines no other Slack tool can produce.
narrative.value_prop: slack-pp-cli wraps the full 174-endpoint Slack Web API and keeps a local SQLite mirror of channels, users, messages, threads, reactions, and usergroups. The mirror powers offline FTS5 search and transcendence verbs — customer-intel-deep joins Slack against co-located Attio, Asana, and Fathom mirrors; dm-engagement and goal-channel-pulse compose cross-source volumes; agent-audit reads the CLI's own DM-access log. Every write verb supports --dry-run for cron safety.
narrative.auth_narrative: Auth is an xoxp Slack user token. Set SLACK_USER_TOKEN, or let the CLI fall back to ~/.claude/slack-user-token.env. A bot token (xoxb) works for post-only flows via SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the token resolves and the workspace is reachable before anything else.
Hydrate the local SQLite mirror — channels, users, messages, threads, reactions, usergroups.
Offline FTS5 search across every synced channel — no rate limit.
The headline verb — a cross-source timeline for one customer.

troubleshoots.symptom: not_authed or invalid_auth on every call
troubleshoots.fix: Confirm SLACK_USER_TOKEN holds a valid xoxp token; run slack-pp-cli doctor to see which source resolved.

troubleshoots.symptom: conversations history returns far fewer messages than --limit requested
troubleshoots.fix: Slack's May-2025 page-size cap may be active for the token; the CLI logs a silent-truncation warning — re-run sync which paginates with Retry-After respect.

troubleshoots.symptom: customer-intel-deep reports a missing sibling mirror
troubleshoots.fix: It needs the pp-attio / pp-asana / pp-fathom SQLite mirrors co-located; run their sync commands or pass --skip-missing to degrade gracefully.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for slack-pp-cli when an agent task needs Slack workspace data composed with history — weekly customer sweeps, L10 prep, pre-1:1 engagement volumes, cron-posted alerts — rather than a single live lookup. Its local mirror makes repeated and offline queries cheap, and its cross-source verbs answer questions no single Slack API call can. For a one-off read of one channel, the Slack MCP is lighter.

recipes.title: Weekly customer sweep
recipes.explanation: Narrows the cross-channel customer timeline to just the fields an agent needs, keeping the payload small.

recipes.title: Pre-1:1 engagement scan
recipes.explanation: One volume row per direct report — DM count, Asana tasks, Fathom calls — for fast 1:1 prep.

recipes.title: Cron-safe alert post
recipes.explanation: Shows the exact request a cron would send without sending it; drop --dry-run to post.

recipes.title: Daily attention pulse
recipes.explanation: Top messages by reaction count plus emoji-class buckets for the channel.
